ing students from across India.

4. TECHNICAL CHAPTERS & STUDENT CLUBS DIRECTORY (INSTITUTE & UNIVERSITY LEVEL)
================================================================================
IMPORTANT NOTE ON CLUB ARCHITECTURE:
At CHARUSAT, student technical chapters and clubs operate centrally at the Institute (CSPIT / DEPSTAR / CMPICA) and University level. Individual departments (such as AI & ML, CE, IT, EC, EE, ME, Civil) do NOT maintain sepa

L, CE, IT, EC, EE, ME, Civil) do NOT maintain separate isolated mini-clubs. Instead, students and faculty coordinators from all engineering departments (including AI & ML) actively collaborate, lead, and organize activities through these official recognized chapters:

• IEEE Student Branch (CHARUSAT IEEE): Active student chapter organizing IEEE conferences, national workshops, and Women in Engineering (WiE) initiatives.
• ACM Student Chapter: Association for Computing Machinery student body focusing on theoretical computing, algorithm seminars, and coding bootcamps.
• CSI Student Chapter (Computer Society of India): Organizes software development, app building, and database design workshops.
• Google Developer Student Clubs (GDSC CHARUSAT): Student community

Student Clubs (GDSC CHARUSAT): Student community for Google technologies (Android, Flutter, Firebase, Google Cloud, TensorFlow).
• AWS Cloud Club & Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors (MLSA): Cloud computing certifications, AWS credits, and Azure workshops.
• Charusat Robotics & IoT Club: Hands-on robotics, ROS, Arduino, ESP32, and Raspberry Pi maker lab.
• Astronomy Club & Stargazing Unit: Stargazing telescope nights, astronomical observation sessions, and space tech workshops affiliated with

essions, and space tech workshops affiliated with the Space Center (CSRTC).
• Competitive Programming Club: Weekly CodeChef, LeetCode, and HackerRank contests.
• Rotaract Club of CHARUSAT / NSS / NCC: Social outreach, blood donation drives, tree plantation, disaster relief, and village digital literacy camps.

• Grading Scale:
  - Grade O (Outstanding): 90% to 100% | Grade Point = 10.0
  - Grade A+ (Excellent): 80% to 89% | Grade Point = 9.0
  - Grade A (Very Good): 70% to 79% | Grade Point = 8.0
  - Grade B+ (Good): 60% to 69% | Grade Point = 7.0
  - Grade B (Above Average)

9% | Grade Point = 7.0
  - Grade B (Above Average): 50% to 59% | Grade Point = 6.0
  - Grade C (Average): 45% to 49% | Grade Point = 5.0
  - Grade P (Pass): 40% to 44% | Grade Point = 4.0
  - Grade F (Fail): Below 40% | Grade Point = 0.0 (Backlog / Remedial required)

• Formula for SGPA (Semester Grade Point Average):
  SGPA = Sum(Course_Credits * Grade_Points) / Sum(Course_Credits)

• Formula for CGPA (Cumulative Grade Point Average):
  CGPA = Sum(All_Semester_Credits * All_Semester_SGPA) / Total_Credits_Attempted

• Percentage Equivalent Formula:
  Percentage (%) = (CGPA - 0.5) * 10 or CGPA * 9.5 (As per university transcript guidelines).
